auth.title: Lab 4: API Authentication
auth.weeks: Keep-alive slots (10-15 min each); one optional 30-45 min exercise
auth.goal: Make every OAuth decision the exam turns into a scenario concrete: JWT consent and impersonation, Confidential vs Public Authorization Code (PKCE), state, refresh tokens and the extended scope, and individual vs admin consent. You already score 70-80% here, so each exercise targets a trap rather than the basics.
setup: Use your developer (demo) account only. All auth hosts in this lab are account-d.docusign.com; production uses account.docusign.com.

In Apps and Keys create (or reuse) a dedicated lab integration key {integrationKey}. Add redirect URI http://localhost:3000/ds/callback (or another local URI you control) and generate an RSA key pair for JWT. Keep the private key in a local file outside any repo.
Note your own {userId} (API Username GUID) and {accountId} from Apps and Keys. Use placeholders in notes; never paste real IDs, secrets or keys into shared files.

Tools: a browser, Postman (or curl) and https://jwt.io only for DECODING a token you created (never paste the private key into a website). The Node quickstart files app/lib/DSJwtAuth.js, app/lib/DSAuthCodeGrant.js and app/jwt_console_project/jwtConsole.js show the same flows in code; read them, do not copy any key or ID from them.
Have a scratch text file open to record what each response contains (expires_in, presence of refresh_token, scopes).

exercises.title: JWT consent URL: signature impersonation
steps: Build the individual consent URL for your lab key (see api).
Open it in a browser while logged in as your demo user and grant consent; note where the browser is redirected and that a ?code= is appended (you do not use it for JWT).
Open the URL a second time and observe that no consent screen is shown (consent is remembered).
Remove impersonation from the scope list and open it again; note that the scopes on the consent screen change.
Optional: revoke the app under Manage Profile > Connected Apps, then repeat to see the consent screen return.
exercises.api:
GET https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth?response_type=code&scope=signature%20impersonation&client_id={integrationKey}&redirect_uri={redirectUri}
(For Maestro / Navigator add their scopes here too, e.g. signature impersonation aow_manage)
observe: The consent screen lists the scopes requested; impersonation is what allows the app to act as the user without them present.
The redirect URI must exactly match one registered on the key, otherwise an error page appears before any consent.
Consent is per user per integration key and is remembered until revoked.
examTraps: JWT always needs consent first, and the consent must include impersonation; a JWT token request without prior consent returns consent_required.
Adding a new scope (e.g. aow_manage) later means consent must be granted again for that scope.
Consent is a one-time browser step; it is not repeated per token request.

exercises.title: Build and sign the JWT assertion, request a token
steps: Write down the header and payload you will sign (see api). Set iat to now and exp to at most one hour later.
Sign it with RS256 using your private key (quickstart DSJwtAuth.js uses the SDK method requestJWTUserToken; any JWT library works).
POST the assertion to the token endpoint.
Record the response fields; check whether a refresh_token is present.
Decode your assertion (not the access token) locally and confirm iss, sub, aud.
observe: Response has access_token, token_type Bearer and expires_in of about 3600 seconds; there is NO refresh_token.
aud is the host name only (no https://); a wrong aud or a clock skewed iat/exp gives an error.
sub is the user GUID, not the email address.
examTraps: JWT grant has no refresh token: when the token nears expiry, create a new assertion and request a new token.
aud differs between demo (account-d.docusign.com) and production (account.docusign.com); it is a Go Live change.
JWT is for system/back-end integrations acting as a user; it needs an RSA key pair, not a client secret.

exercises.title: /oauth/userinfo and the base_uri
steps: Call userinfo with the token from the previous exercise.
Find the accounts array, the is_default flag and base_uri.
Build the eSignature base path {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{accountId} and make one cheap call (GET .../envelopes?from_date={recentDate}) to prove it works.
Note that Navigator and Maestro use a different host (api-d.docusign.com) rather than base_uri.
exercises.api:
GET https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/userinfo
Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}
observe: base_uri is per account (e.g. a demo host) and must be read, not hard-coded.
A user may belong to several accounts; choose by account_id or is_default.
userinfo is called on the auth host, not on base_uri.
examTraps: Hard-coding base_uri breaks in production or when an account moves; always derive it from /oauth/userinfo and cache it.
accountId comes from userinfo (or Apps and Keys), not from the token itself.
Calling userinfo on every API request wastes quota: call once per token/session.

exercises.title: Confidential Authorization Code Grant with state
steps: Add a secret to your lab key (Apps and Keys > Add Secret). Copy it to a local file only.
Generate a random state value and save it in your scratch file.
Open the authorization URL (see api), log in and consent; copy code and state from the redirect.
Compare the returned state with your saved value; then exchange the code within a few minutes.
Try exchanging the same code twice and note the error the second time.
observe: The token response contains access_token (expires_in about 8 hours) AND refresh_token.
The authorization code is single use and short lived.
state comes back unchanged; your app must reject a callback whose state it did not issue (CSRF protection).
examTraps: Confidential Auth Code is for apps with a back end that can keep the secret; the secret is sent only server-to-server in the Basic header.
state is for CSRF protection, not for authentication of the user.
Auth Code Grant is for a user present in the browser; it is the wrong answer for an unattended nightly job (that is JWT).

exercises.title: Public Authorization Code Grant with PKCE (S256)
steps: Create a second lab key (or change a test key) whose authentication method is Public (no secret). Public keys cannot have a secret.
Generate a code_verifier (43-128 random URL-safe characters) and compute code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) without padding (e.g. node -e with crypto, or an offline PKCE generator).
Open the authorization URL with code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256.
Exchange the code sending code_verifier and client_id in the body and NO Authorization header.
Repeat the exchange with a wrong code_verifier and record the error.
exercises.api:
GET https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth?response_type=code&scope=signature&client_id={integrationKey}&redirect_uri={redirectUri}&state={randomState}&code_challenge={codeChallenge}&code_challenge_method=S256
POST https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant_type=authorization_code&code={code}&client_id={integrationKey}&code_verifier={codeVerifier}
observe: Token exchange succeeds only when SHA256 of the verifier matches the challenge sent earlier.
No secret is used anywhere: the verifier proves that the same client that started the flow finishes it.
For a browser SPA calling eSignature directly, the key also needs CORS configured and the cors scope (read-only note; not required for this exercise).
examTraps: SPA or native/mobile app that cannot hide a secret: Public Authorization Code Grant + PKCE, not Implicit and not Confidential.
code_challenge goes in the authorization request; code_verifier goes in the token request. Swapping them is a classic distractor.
Docusign recommends Public Auth Code over Implicit Grant for SPAs; moving from Implicit requires a new integration key.

exercises.title: Refresh tokens and the extended scope
steps: Using the refresh_token from the Confidential exercise, call the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token.
Compare the new refresh_token with the old one and note the expires_in on the new access token.
Write in your scratch file what changes when the original authorization did or did not include extended.
exercises.api:
POST https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/token
Authorization: Basic base64({integrationKey}:{secretKey})
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={refreshToken}
observe: A new access token is issued without the user logging in again.
Store the refresh token returned by each refresh (treat it as rotating).
Refresh tokens exist only for Authorization Code flows, never for JWT.
examTraps: Without extended the refresh token expires 30 days after original issue; with extended the 30 days are counted from the last refresh (rolling).
Need for long-lived user access without re-login: Auth Code + extended + refresh, not 'request a longer access token'.
Revoking consent invalidates refresh tokens; existing access tokens live until they expire.

exercises.title: Optional (30-45 min): individual vs admin consent decision drill
steps: Read (inspection only; a demo account normally lacks Docusign Admin with a claimed domain) the Docusign pages 'Obtain and revoke consent', 'How to obtain admin consent for internal applications' and '... for external applications'.
In Docusign Admin of your demo org (if visible), look for Domains and Connected Apps / applications pages and note what is missing without a claimed domain.
Write the external-app admin consent URL shape: scope=openid plus admin_consent_scope listing the API scopes, and note who must log in (an org admin).

For five scenarios decide individual vs admin consent: (1) internal HR system using JWT for 2,000 employees; (2) ISV app installed by many customers; (3) one service user for a nightly job; (4) customer org forbids users granting consent themselves; (5) user on a claimed domain tries to revoke consent individually.
Write one fallback rule: always handle consent_required by sending the user to individual consent.
exercises.api:
Inspection only. Individual: GET https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth?response_type=code&scope=signature%20impersonation&client_id={integrationKey}&redirect_uri={redirectUri}
Admin consent (external app): same endpoint with scope=openid and admin_consent_scope={space-separated API scopes} (verify exact parameters on the 'admin consent for external applications' page before relying on them).
observe: Admin consent needs Docusign Admin (Access Management) and a claimed domain; it grants consent for all users of that domain at once.
Users on a reserved/claimed domain cannot revoke admin-granted consent individually; it is revoked in Docusign Admin.
Internal apps (key owned by your org) are consented in Docusign Admin; external apps use the special-scope URL.
examTraps: Many users impersonated by one JWT app: admin consent is the scalable answer; a single service user only needs individual consent once.
Admin consent is not available without a claimed domain; the correct design keeps an individual-consent fallback.
Consent is not the same as account permissions: a consented user still needs the account rights for the API action.

cleanup: Delete the lab secret from the integration key if you no longer need it, and delete the test RSA key pair or keep it only locally.
Revoke the lab app under Manage Profile > Connected Apps if you want to re-run the consent exercises from scratch.
Delete any scratch file that contains tokens, secrets or codes.
takeaways: Unattended back-end job acting as a user: JWT Grant, consent first with signature impersonation, no refresh token.
Web app with a server and a user present: Confidential Authorization Code Grant with a secret sent only server-side.
SPA or mobile app: Public Authorization Code Grant with PKCE (S256), no secret; CORS needs the cors scope.
Always send and verify state on the authorization redirect.
Need long-lived access without re-login: refresh tokens plus the extended scope (rolling 30 days).
Derive base_uri and accountId from /oauth/userinfo once per session; never hard-code them.
Request only the scopes the calls need (signature, aow_manage, adm_store_unified_repo_read, webforms_*); adding a scope means new consent.
Admin consent requires Docusign Admin and a claimed domain; keep individual consent as a fallback for consent_required.

agreement_manager.title: Lab 7: Agreement Manager API
agreement_manager.weeks: Keep-alive slots (10-15 min each); one optional 30-45 min exercise
agreement_manager.goal: Use the Agreement Manager (Navigator) API exactly as the exam frames it: list and filter AI-extracted agreements, read one agreement's provisions, request an AI summary, and design how extracted values flow into an external system. Remember the API surface is small: GetAgreementsList, GetAgreement, DeleteAgreement and CreateAgreementSummary only.
setup: Demo account only. The account must have Agreement Manager / Navigator enabled with some agreements in the repository (the Navigator beta seeded demo accounts with test data; if the Agreements screen is empty, upload 2-3 sample PDFs through the web app UI, because the API has no upload operation).
Base path: https://api-d.docusign.com/v1 (demo) and https://api.docusign.com/v1 (production). This is NOT the eSignature base_uri.
Get a token (JWT or Auth Code from Lab 4) with scope signature adm_store_unified_repo_read; re-consent if the key was consented without it.

Postman with the Docusign Navigator collection or plain curl works; the project folder navigator-integration/server.js and the quickstart app/lib/navigator/examples/listAgreements.js and getSingleAgreement.js show the same calls. Do not copy any key or ID from them.

exercises.title: First call: GetAgreementsList and the scope trap
steps: Call GetAgreementsList with limit=5.
Repeat with a token that has only signature (no adm_store_unified_repo_read) and record the status code.
In the successful response, note for one entry: id, type, category, status, parties, provisions, source_name, metadata.created_at.
observe: Agreements come back under a data array with AI-extracted provisions already included in each entry.
Without the Navigator scope the call is rejected (401/403); adding the scope requires new consent before JWT tokens work again.
The host is api-d.docusign.com, not your account's eSignature base_uri.
examTraps: Agreement Manager API uses its own base path (api-d / api .docusign.com/v1) and the adm_store_unified_repo_read scope.
Adding a scope to the JWT payload without re-consenting gives consent_required.
Agreement data is read with Agreement Manager, not with eSignature Envelopes:get (an envelope is not an extracted agreement).

exercises.title: Filters and paging
steps: Filter agreements expiring in the next year: provisions.expiration_date with gte and lte operators.
Filter by party name with parties.name_in_agreement and by status.
Add sort and direction (asc/desc).
Call with limit=2, find the continuation token in the response and call again passing it as ctoken until no more pages.
observe: Supported filters include id, status, title, parties.name_in_agreement, metadata.created_at, provisions.effective_date / expiration_date / execution_date / term_length, languages, source_name, source_id.
term_length uses ISO 8601 durations (P1Y), dates use ISO 8601 dates.
Paging is token based (limit + ctoken), not start_position/count as in eSignature lists.
examTraps: 'Find contracts renewing in the next 90 days' is a GetAgreementsList filter on provision dates, not a loop of GetAgreement calls.
Do not assume eSignature paging parameters on this API; use limit and ctoken.
Filter server-side instead of downloading everything and filtering in your app.

exercises.title: GetAgreement for one ID
steps: Pick an id from the list and call GetAgreement.
Compare its provisions with the same entry in the list response.

Note fields useful for an external system: provisions.renewal_type, renewal_notice_date, total_agreement_value + currency code, governing_law, related_agreement_documents.parent_agreement_document_id, source_id.
exercises.api:
GET https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements/{agreementId}
Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}
observe: Durations (term_length, renewal_notice_period) are ISO 8601 strings like P3Y or P90D; values may be SILENT when the document does not say.
source_name / source_id tell you where the agreement came from (e.g. Docusign eSign) so you can link back.
related_agreement_documents links an amendment to its parent agreement.
examTraps: Use GetAgreement for one known ID; use GetAgreementsList for searching.
There is no getAgreementSummary operation; a summary is created with POST .../ai/actions/summarize.
Provision values are AI-extracted and can be corrected by a human in the UI, so do not treat them as legally binding.

exercises.title: CreateAgreementSummary (AI summarize action)
steps: POST to the summarize action for the same agreement (no body needed beyond headers).
Read the summary and check it against two provision values you saw in GetAgreement.
Note the method (POST) and that invoking it accepts the Docusign AI terms.
observe: 200 returns a JSON object containing the AI-generated summary.
The summary is a concise overview that may miss details or legal nuance; the original document stays the binding source.
If you get 403, check plan/feature availability and the scopes on the token (see 'Navigator Authentication' in the docs for the full scope list).
examTraps: Summary = POST .../ai/actions/summarize (CreateAgreementSummary); a GET of a summary does not exist.
Do not store an AI summary as the contract of record; link to the agreement and keep human review.
Summaries are on demand per agreement, not returned by the list call.

exercises.title: Map extracted provisions to an external system
steps: Design (on paper) a CRM/ERP sync: which fields from GetAgreementsList map to which CRM fields (id -> external key, parties -> account, expiration_date / renewal_notice_date -> renewal task, total_agreement_value + currency -> opportunity value).
Decide the trigger: a scheduled job using a metadata.created_at filter since the last run, or an event from your own system; write down why you would not poll every agreement by ID.
Decide how to store the Agreement Manager id and source_id so you can re-read later.
Decide which fields need human review before they drive money or legal actions.
exercises.api:
GET https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements?metadata.created_at[gte]={lastRunDate}&limit=50
then for paging: &ctoken={ctoken}
observe: Incremental sync is possible with created_at / date filters plus paging.
Values corrected by a user in the UI are returned instead of the original AI values on the next GET, so a re-sync picks up corrections.
The API currently reads data; updates of extracted values are done in the UI.
examTraps: Sync to CRM/ERP: list with filters + paging, store the agreement id, re-read; do not scrape documents yourself.
Feeding a copilot/LLM with agreement data is a documented use case of the list operation.
Least privilege: a read-only sync needs only the read scope, not write/admin scopes.

exercises.title: Review AI-extracted values in the UI
steps: Open the agreement in the Agreements screen of the web app and find its extracted fields.
Correct one value (e.g. renewal notice period) if your account allows edits.
Call GetAgreement again and compare.
Note which role in your organization should own this review.
exercises.api: GET https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements/{agreementId} (before and after the UI edit)
observe: After a user edit, the API returns the user-updated value instead of the AI-extracted value.
Custom agreement types reduce agreements classified as Other; fields on a type can be AI-detected.
Legacy (non-Docusign) agreements uploaded into the repository are extracted the same way.
examTraps: AI extraction needs human review for high-impact fields; the exam favours 'review then act' over fully automatic action.
Corrections are made by users (UI) and then visible through the API.
Misclassified agreements: create a custom agreement type rather than post-processing in code.

exercises.title: Optional (30-45 min): small sync script plus DeleteAgreement decision
steps: Run navigator-integration/server.js locally (fill your own local .env, never commit it) or adapt the quickstart listAgreements example to print id, type, expiration_date and renewal_notice_date for all pages.
Write the output as CSV to simulate an import into a CRM.
Read the DeleteAgreement reference (DELETE /v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements/{agreementId}) and decide when, if ever, your integration should call it; do NOT delete seeded data you still need.
List three failure cases (401 expired token, 403 missing scope/feature, 429 rate limit) and the handling for each.
exercises.api:
GET https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements?limit=50[&ctoken=...]
DELETE https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/agreements/{agreementId} (read only; do not run on data you need)
observe: All pages are fetched by following ctoken until none is returned.
Only four operations exist; anything else in an exam option (update provisions, upload document, get summary) is a distractor for this API.
Token refresh/renewal from Lab 4 applies unchanged.
examTraps: There is no upload or update endpoint in this API version; uploads and corrections happen in the UI.
Deleting an agreement is destructive and rarely the answer to a sync scenario.
Handle 401 by getting a new token, 403 by checking scope/consent/plan, 429 by backing off.

cleanup: Delete local CSV exports and any .env file with credentials when done.
Revert any UI edits to extracted values if you want the original AI values for future labs.
takeaways: Agreement Manager API base path is api-d.docusign.com/v1 (demo) / api.docusign.com/v1 (prod), separate from the eSignature base_uri.
Scope adm_store_unified_repo_read is required to read agreements; adding it means new consent.
Search = GetAgreementsList with filters (dates, parties, status, type, source) and limit + ctoken paging.
One agreement = GetAgreement by id; AI summary = POST .../ai/actions/summarize (CreateAgreementSummary).
Only GetAgreementsList, GetAgreement, DeleteAgreement and CreateAgreementSummary exist; there is no getAgreementSummary.
AI-extracted values and summaries need human review; user corrections in the UI replace AI values in API responses.
Sync to CRM/ERP by filtered, paged reads keyed on the agreement id, not by parsing documents yourself.

embedding.title: Lab 8: Embedding - redirect vs iframe vs Docusign JS
embedding.weeks: Keep-alive slots (10-15 min each); one optional 30-45 min exercise
embedding.goal: Use the quiz app's Embedding lab page (http://127.0.0.1:5173) to show the same Docusign URL as a full-page redirect, a plain iframe and Docusign JS, and learn what each requires. Covers embedded signing classic vs focused view, embedded sending, web form instances, workflow instance URLs, returnUrl events vs sessionEnd, the 5-minute single-use URL and why Connect, not the browser, confirms completion.
setup: Demo account only. Start the quiz app (npm run dev in quiz-app) and open the Embedding lab page at http://127.0.0.1:5173.
Have a token with signature (and webforms_read webforms_instance_read webforms_instance_write for web forms, aow_manage for Maestro) from Lab 4, plus {accountId} and {base_uri} from /oauth/userinfo.
Enter your {integrationKey} in the Embedding lab page (Docusign JS needs it for loadDocuSign).

Origins: frameAncestors must list your page origin AND https://apps-d.docusign.com; messageOrigins must be https://apps-d.docusign.com (the Docusign origin, not yours). The page shows http://127.0.0.1:5173 as your origin. The docs only exempt http://localhost from the HTTPS requirement, so if 127.0.0.1 is refused, open the page as http://localhost:5173 and use that origin instead.

Reference code: quickstart app/lib/eSignature/examples/focusedView.js (eg044), eg001EmbeddedSigning.js, eg011EmbeddedSending.js, app/lib/webforms/examples/createInstance.js, app/lib/maestro/examples/triggerWorkflow.js. Do not copy any key or ID from them.
Every view URL expires 5 minutes after creation and works once: create it, paste it into the page immediately, and create a new one for each display mode.

exercises.title: Embedded signer envelope + classic view by redirect
steps: Create and send an envelope (status sent) with one signer that has clientUserId set (any value unique in the envelope, e.g. 1001).
Call createRecipient with the SAME email, userName and clientUserId plus a returnUrl that points to your page (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:5173/?view=return).
Paste the url into the Embedding lab and choose full-page redirect; sign.
Read the event query parameter appended to the returnUrl.
Create a second URL and decline or cancel instead; compare the event values.
observe: The signer receives no email from Docusign because clientUserId marks them as embedded.
After signing the browser lands on returnUrl?event=signing_complete; other values include cancel, decline, session_timeout, ttl_expired, viewing_complete, access_code_failed.
createRecipient fails if email/userName/clientUserId do not match the recipient, or if the envelope is not in sent status.
examTraps: Embedded signing needs clientUserId on the recipient at send time; without it you cannot generate a recipient view.
Recipient view URLs are only for sent envelopes; a draft uses createSender (embedded sending).
returnUrl event values are hints for the UI, not proof of completion.

exercises.title: 5-minute single-use URL
steps: Create a recipient view URL and paste it into the page in redirect mode; then paste the SAME URL again.
Create another URL and wait more than 5 minutes before opening it.
Record what you see in both cases and the event reported.
exercises.api: POST {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{accountId}/envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/recipient (same body as before)
observe: Observe whether the reused or expired URL shows an error page or returns to returnUrl with event=ttl_expired (documented meaning: token not used within the timeout or already accessed).
A new URL must be generated each time the user (re)opens signing.
The signing session itself has a separate inactivity timeout (session_timeout).
examTraps: Never email or store a recipient view URL; generate it on demand right before redirecting the user.
'Signer clicks the link tomorrow' is not possible with an embedded URL: generate a fresh one when they return to your app.
ttl_expired (URL not used in time or reused) is different from session_timeout (inactive in the session).

exercises.title: Plain iframe vs focused view with Docusign JS
steps: Create a recipient view with frameAncestors and messageOrigins (see api) and open it in mode 2, plain iframe; note what happens.
Create a new URL with the same body and open it in mode 3, Docusign JS (signing with displayFormat focused); sign and watch the event log.
Create a URL WITHOUT frameAncestors/messageOrigins and try mode 3 again; record the failure.
Create a URL with frameAncestors missing your origin (only https://apps-d.docusign.com) and try mode 3 again.
observe: With correct origins, Docusign JS creates the iframe itself, raises ready when displayed and sessionEnd (sessionEndType signing_complete, cancel, decline, ttl_expired, ...) at the end, then removes the iframe; no browser redirect happens.
With origins missing, observe whether the frame is blocked (browser console shows a frame-ancestors/CSP refusal) or the session never becomes ready.
In the plain iframe, observe whether the classic session loads and whether, at the end, the returnUrl opens inside the frame (your page nested in itself).
examTraps: Focused view requires Docusign JS plus frameAncestors (your origin + apps-d/apps.docusign.com) and messageOrigins (apps-d/apps.docusign.com).
Focused view only works inside an iframe that Docusign JS builds; it ends with DOM events, not a redirect.
Production uses https://apps.docusign.com and HTTPS-only origins; demo values do not carry over.

exercises.title: Which features force classic view
steps: Create an envelope whose embedded signer needs ID verification (or a payment tab) if your demo account allows it; otherwise do this as a reading exercise in 'Embedded signing' concepts.
Try to open it in focused view; then open a new URL in classic view by redirect.
Write a decision table: requirement -> classic redirect / classic with Docusign JS / focused view.
exercises.api: Same createRecipient call; envelope signer with identityVerification {"workflowId":"{idvWorkflowId}"} or a payment tab (only if enabled in your demo account).
observe: Documented: focused view does not yet support payment tabs, ID verification, or some SBS pen providers; classic view supports the most authentication options (access code, KBA, IDV).
Classic in an iframe is not supported for all authentication options or SBS pen types; mobile signers need full-screen iframes.
Classic view can also be rendered through Docusign JS to get DOM events.
examTraps: IDV, payments or SBS in an embedded flow: choose classic view (redirect), not focused view.
Want minimal UI inside your page and none of those features: focused view with Docusign JS.
Click to Agree (focused view with no tabs) needs Document Visibility off on the account.

exercises.title: Embedded sending with createSender
steps: Create an envelope with status created (draft) and one remote signer.
Call createSender with a returnUrl and open the URL in redirect mode.
Change a tab or recipient in the sender view and send.
Try createSender on an already sent envelope and record the result.
observe: The sender view lets your user prepare and send inside your app; the return lands on returnUrl with an event value (e.g. Send or Save).
The envelope status moves from created to sent only when the user sends.
Sender view URLs also expire quickly; create on demand.
examTraps: Let a user review/tag before sending inside your app: draft envelope (status created) + createSender, not createRecipient.
createRecipient = signer experience; createSender = sender/prepare experience.
Embedded sending does not make the recipients embedded; that still depends on clientUserId.

exercises.title: Web form instance: embedded vs remote, and a workflow instance URL
steps: Pick an active template-based web form ({formId}) and create an embedded instance with clientUserId and formValues.
Paste formUrl and instanceToken into the page; open in mode 3 (webforms with options.instanceToken) and in redirect mode (formUrl#instanceToken=...) using new instances.
Create a remote instance (sendOption now + recipients with roleName) and note that there is no URL to embed; the recipient gets email.
If you have a published Maestro workflow started From an API call, call TriggerWorkflow and paste instance_url into redirect and iframe modes.
observe: instanceToken expires 5 minutes after creation even though the instance itself lives until tokenExpirationDateTime / expirationOffset; an expired one shows 'Unable to load form'.
Docusign JS webforms(...) raises ready, userActivity and sessionEnd events; redirecting leaves your app.

Workflow instance_url: redirect leaves the user on Docusign after completion; iframe keeps your app around it. Embedded workflows support From a Link / From an API call starts, do not support Collect Data from an ID, and do not support focused view for the signature step.
examTraps: Remote web form delivery needs sendOption + recipient/roleName values and does not work with standalone forms or attachment fields.
Embedded web form: clientUserId + Docusign JS (recommended) using formUrl and instanceToken.
Embedded Maestro instance: iframe the instance_url, choose From an API call when passing starting variables.

exercises.title: Optional (30-45 min): never trust the browser - confirm with Connect
steps: Set up a webhook.site URL and add an envelope-level eventNotification (or use your Lab 3 account-level Connect configuration) for recipient-completed and envelope-completed.
Run one embedded signing in focused view; record when sessionEnd fires and when the Connect message arrives.
Run another and close the browser tab right after clicking Finish; check that Connect still reports completion.
Manually open your returnUrl with ?event=signing_complete on an unsigned envelope and note that your app would be fooled if it trusted that value.
Write the rule your back end follows: update business state only from Connect (or a GET of envelope status), use returnUrl/sessionEnd only to change the UI.
exercises.api:
In the envelope body: "eventNotification":{"url":"{webhookSiteUrl}","requireAcknowledgment":"true","includeHMAC":"true","eventData":{"version":"restv2.1","format":"json"},"events":["recipient-completed","envelope-completed"]}
(Verify field names against your Lab 3 notes or API Explorer.)
observe: Connect delivers completion even when the browser never returns to your app.
returnUrl parameters can be cancelled, closed or spoofed; the docs explicitly say not to rely on them.
sessionEnd is a DOM event in the user's browser and has the same weakness.
examTraps: Completion must be confirmed server-side (Connect or GET envelope), never from returnUrl or sessionEnd alone.
Do not poll per envelope more than once every 15 minutes; Connect is the scalable answer.
Verify HMAC on Connect messages before trusting them.

cleanup: Void or let expire any in-flight test envelopes; delete draft envelopes from the sender exercise.
Remove the envelope-level webhook URL from your notes and delete the webhook.site bin.
Stop the quiz app dev server; do not commit any token or integration key entered in the page.
takeaways: Embedded signer = clientUserId at send time + createRecipient with the same identity; the envelope must be sent.
Embedded sending = draft envelope (status created) + createSender.
View URLs expire in 5 minutes and are single use: generate on demand, never store or email them.
Focused view = Docusign JS + frameAncestors (your origin + apps-d/apps.docusign.com) + messageOrigins (apps-d/apps.docusign.com); ends with sessionEnd events, not a redirect.
Need IDV, payments or some SBS: use classic view (redirect is the safest).
Embedded web form = clientUserId + formUrl + instanceToken via Docusign JS; remote = sendOption + recipients with roleName.
Workflow instance_url can be redirected or iframed; embedded workflows cannot use Collect Data from an ID or focused view signing.
returnUrl events and sessionEnd drive the UI only; confirm completion with Connect or the API.
